Short frames see approximately frozen speed offsets. Long frames see effective
phase diffusion. If every frame lies in only one regime, $\lambda_r$ will be
weakly identified.

## 8.3 Telemetry, and the three distinct speed quantities

Three different speed quantities appear in this work. They are not
interchangeable, and the entire comparison protocol depends on keeping their
names apart.

| Name | What it is | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **raw telemetry reference** | the exogenous published raw array | **the** primary scoring reference, the identical array for the real arm and for every synthetic arm; reported as *reference agreement*, never as proven ground truth; never switched between arms |
| **refined / posterior track** | any inferred trajectory, including the `rps_key rps_refined` recorded in the existing exports | fit provenance and diagnostics only; never a scoring reference, never a held-out predictive input |
| **realized physical shaft RPS** | the renderer's exact $f_{\text{true}}$ label (§7.1) | diagnostic MAE only; never a gate, never the primary target |

:::: {.callout-important}
## This is a human convention, and it is frozen before any comparison

The mathematics separates the exogenous reference trajectory from the
renderer's realized physical shaft speed. It cannot decide which of them the
frozen tracker's existing MAE convention is *intended* to call its target. That
choice is an unavoidable human convention, and it is frozen in the manifest
before any arm is scored: candidate and real agreement are reported against the
same raw reference. Switching the primary target to $f_{\text{true}}$ would
answer a *different* supervised-task question, even though $f_{\text{true}}$ is
the physically exact render label.
::::

If tachometer or controller telemetry is available at adequate rate, it may
additionally be included as another noisy observation of the latent $\nu_r(t)$.
That anchors the shared state and tests whether the acoustic common factor is
genuinely shaft motion rather than a shared acoustic or electronic disturbance.
It is an option, not part of C2.

## 8.4 The latent state grid is not the spectral window

The latent $(\theta,\nu)$ grid is chosen from the **phase-dynamics bandwidth**,
independently of the STFT window and hop. Overlap between analysis frames does
not resolve subwindow dynamics (§6.2): overlapping frames re-use the same
samples, they do not add a faster observation of the state. This is why §8.2's
advice about useful frame lengths is about *identifiability of the dynamics*,
not about how finely the state is represented.

:::: {.callout-warning}
## Interpolating between grid points omits the OU bridge variance

Conditioning only on dense-grid MAP endpoints and interpolating between them
**omits the integrated-OU bridge variance** between grid points. This is
labelled a **grid approximation**, and C2 must demonstrate
convergence as $\Delta_{\text{state}}$ shrinks at fixed STFT hop and window.
Including an exact Gaussian bridge covariance in the kernel would remove the
approximation; that is listed as optional future complexity (§13) and is not
the default. Neither choice forces full complex smoothing.
::::

# 9. Correctness checks required before the model is believed

Every check must exercise both inference and rendering. None of them is a
performance measurement; they are the conditions under which the numbers of a
fit mean anything at all.

1. **Exact integrated-OU moments.** Planted $(\theta,\nu)$ covariance against
   the known covariance, including the near-zero $\lambda\Delta$ limit, with
   correlated $\theta$/$\nu$ increments produced by **one shared state**.
2. **Phase covariance decomposition.** Shaft-only ($D_g=0$), independent-only
   ($\sigma_{\nu,r}=0$) and combined planted phase covariance; the $k$ loading
   and the order-normalised differences. Biased-carrier plus bias/OU ambiguity
   is **reported**, and the deliberate two-path Hessian gauge-direction check
   of §6.1.1 belongs to this item.
3. **Conditional versus marginal.** A nearly perfectly observed planted shaft
   path ($C_{\text{post}}\to0$) must remove the OU broadening from the
   conditional spectrum while the marginal prediction stays correct; plus
   $D_g=0$ MAP-path recovery and $\theta_r=0$ scalar-$D_g$ recovery.
4. **Finite-window power.** Pure tone and planted chirp finite-window power
   including fractional bins, the floor, and the phase units. The zero-noise
   limit must return exactly the window response, including its nulls and its
   fractional-bin offset.
5. **Subwindow motion and grid convergence.** The subwindow-oscillation line
   of §6.2, and state-grid convergence as $\Delta_{\text{state}}$ shrinks at
   fixed STFT hop and window (§8.4).
6. **Exposure.** Overlap duplicates create no exposure and no information, and
   no held-out raw-sample support leaks through window or filter support.
7. **Render label.** The generated physical RPS integrates to the shared
   phase, excludes $\epsilon$, and has the same timeline and length as the
   audio after resampling (§7.1).
8. **Near crossings.** C2 is tested on the **continuously summed
   spectral components that share the same $\theta$**, plus the companion
   harmonics of both rotors: no nearest-bin classification, and no forced
   allocation when the pair is unidentifiable — unresolved overlaps are
   excluded from the moment initializer instead. Missing/weak-order gates are
   declared **before** estimates. A crossing check on **joint complex
   observations** requires the optional complex state-space /
   $\epsilon$-latent likelihood (§13) and is reserved for a future candidate
   that implements it; C2 marginalizes $\epsilon$ and never forms
   that likelihood.
9. **Gradients.** Finite parameter and device gradients across the whole
   objective.
10. **Only if a sparse method is ever introduced.** Small-$K$ sparse against a
    dense reference, on both objective value and recovery — with **no**
    exact-$O(K)$ assertion (§6.1.6).

Retained from the earlier list, unchanged in substance: one physical parameter
vector must fit several STFT lengths with only the observation window changing;
low-SNR cells must either stay calibrated under the complex-observation model
or be excluded by a fixed rule; shaft parameters must be recoverable from a
non-consecutive set of orders; two rotors must each keep their own rank-one
block, and nearby crossing lines must not create false covariance; a
fit-to-render round trip must recover the exported parameters; and posterior
predictive checks compare spectra, centre-bin distributions, phase structure
functions, cross-order covariance and tracker error.

Only a genuinely uncertain behavioural risk earns a retained regression test.
A successful mean-spectrum fit is necessary but not sufficient.

# 10. Reinterpretation of the existing bench findings

The earlier measurements should be retained, with the following changes in
language.

## 10.1 Findings that remain valid

- Low orders are much narrower and have more stable centre-bin magnitudes than
  high orders.
- A single fitted Lorentzian per line is inadequate.
- The STFT window must be represented exactly.
- Narrow width floors censor the fit and must remain removed.
- The $\pm6$ Hz measurement band censored high-order equivalent widths.
- Analysis and rendering must use the same resampling path.
- Static bench clips should not be fitted with unnecessary amplitude dynamics.
- Blind bench-to-flight transfer remains a valid and important end-to-end test.

## 10.2 Claims that should be withdrawn or softened

Replace these claims:

- ``the coherent fraction is real'';
- ``every order holds a deterministic tone and stochastic pedestal'';
- ``the renderer fits the same physics by splitting the power into two paths'';
- ``the two-component likelihood proves a physical mixture''.

Use these claims instead:

- the mean spectrum strongly supports at least two apparent linewidth scales;
- a narrow-plus-broad template predicts the measured spectrum better than one
  Lorentzian;
- this template is phenomenological until cross-harmonic phase tests establish
  the underlying dynamics;
- integrated-OU shaft speed plus independent per-harmonic phase diffusion is a
  physical candidate that predicts both marginal line shapes and joint phase
  statistics.

## 10.3 The old $k$-linear pedestal width is not a physical law

The measured equivalent width can grow approximately linearly with $k$ over a
finite range even when the model's asymptotic central linewidth contains a
$k^2$ shaft term. Equivalent width is not HWHM. It depends on the entire line,
the window, the floor subtraction, and the measurement band.

Therefore retain the observed $k$-linear trend as a descriptive statistic. Do
not force the physical model to reproduce it through a linearly parameterised
Lorentzian width. Instead, pass the physical line through the exact measurement
pipeline and compare the resulting equivalent widths.

# 11. Revised implementation plan

C2 is the smallest member of the family above, and the campaign
ledger for it is `docs/experiments/revised-phase-campaign.qmd`. The order of
work follows from two hard constraints: **no candidate fit happens before the
frozen baseline evaluator is approved and the manifest is frozen**, and the
cheap falsifications come first.

## Phase 1: diagnostics without changing the production fit

1. Add extraction of complex, **raw**-telemetry-demodulated harmonic tracks.
2. Plot phase structure functions for every reliable order.
3. Plot $\widehat{\operatorname{Cov}}(\Delta\psi_k,\Delta\psi_l)/(kl)$ across
   order pairs and lags.
4. Plot order-normalised phase-difference structure functions.
5. Check whether the common covariance is rank one and whether its leading
   eigenvector is proportional to $k$.

This phase can falsify the proposed mechanism before any spectral change. The
flight carrier is the **raw** label plus the fitted per-clip bias; demodulating
with the refined label is a diagnostic comparison only (§6.1.1).

## Phase 2: moment initialisation

1. Implement the integrated-OU structure function with its stable small-lag
   form.
2. Estimate the rig parameters $\lambda_g,\sigma_g$ from off-diagonal covariance
   on the preregistered isolated high-SNR support, and **freeze them** for
   C2.
3. Initialise the scalar $D_g$ from the diagonal residuals; §6.2 then fits it
   inside the one spectral composite MAP. Negative raw estimates are
   observations, not zeros (§6.1.5).
4. Take uncertainty from a moving-block bootstrap over contiguous time blocks,
   never from a pair count.
5. Run the §9 checks that cover these estimators.

## Phase 3: one composite MAP objective

1. Implement $R_k(\tau)$, the windowed-correlation transform (§6.2.1) and the
   conditional double-window atom (§6.2), sharing **one** finite-window
   convention between both expected-spectrum paths.
2. Normalise every line to unit integrated power.
3. Fit the per-clip bias, the dense-grid shared $(\theta_r,\nu_r)$ path, the
   scalar $D_g$, the existing line and floor powers and the tied speed law in
   **one** ordinary-Adam MAP pass, under one exact Gaussian integrated-OU
   state prior.
4. Keep the one-Cauchy and two-Cauchy variants as descriptive baselines,
   **rescored** — never refitted — under the identical observation protocol.
5. Compare with the frozen overlap-aware composite risk of §6.2.3.

## Phase 4: renderer and evaluation

1. Implement the exact discrete-time shared shaft transition and the render
   contract of §7.1, including the uniform initial residual phases and the
   realized shaft label.
2. Confirm fit-to-render parameter units with round-trip tests.
3. Run the frozen evaluator on the frozen manifest. The gates of §12 decide;
   a visually convincing spectrum does not.

Ownership: the candidate model, its script and its tests are implemented by
the candidate-implementation worker, and the evaluator plus the render
anti-aliasing path belong to the baseline/evaluation worker. This document
specifies the science, not the file contents.

# 12. Model comparison and acceptance criteria

Two different things were previously conflated in this section, and they are
now separate: a **descriptive model-comparison ladder**, which is how the
mechanism is understood, and the **frozen acceptance gate**, which is what
decides whether a candidate passes.

## 12.1 The descriptive ladder — explicitly not the gate

| Variant | Purpose |
|---|---|
| One Lorentzian per order | Minimal spectral baseline |
| Positive narrow + broad Cauchy | Flexible descriptive baseline |
| Integrated-OU shaft only | Tests whether common rotor motion is sufficient |
| Integrated-OU shaft + independent diffusion | The proposed physical mechanism |

Use held-out clips or contiguous held-out time blocks behind a window/filter
support guard. Do not randomly hold out overlapping STFT cells. Old exports are
**rescored**, never refitted, and a smoothed observed periodogram is not a
model prediction.

Diagnostically, the mechanism is supported only if it predicts the observed
cross-order covariance without fitting each pair, if order-normalised
differences remove the fitted shaft component, if one set of physical dynamics
works across window lengths, and if rendered audio reproduces the phase,
spectral and centre-bin statistics of real audio. If the spectrum improves but
the covariance test fails, the result is another useful line-shape
parameterisation, not a validated shared-shaft model.

## 12.2 The frozen acceptance gate

:::: {.callout-important}
## The authoritative ledger is the campaign document

`docs/experiments/revised-phase-campaign.qmd` holds the frozen criteria, the
round ledger and the evidence policy. The summary below must not drift from it,
and no threshold is ever moved to let a model through.
::::

**DREGON — cruise only.** The frozen real-trained HPPNet L2 tracker
(`hppnet_l2_r2_s0`, best checkpoint, its actual digest pinned in the manifest)
scores PIT MAE on matched real and on baseline/candidate synthetic. The
positive real-synthetic gap is calibrated **first**. The point target is

$$
E_{\text{new}}\le E_{\text{real}}
+0.70\left(E_{\text{best synth}}-E_{\text{real}}\right),
$$

a closure of at least 30 % of that gap, and the one-sided 95 % cluster
interval must exclude no improvement. Clusters are **independently recorded
trajectory sessions** — the five no-source room2 cruise recordings — and
explicitly not different physical aircraft, channels, windows or render seeds;
resampling is matched and paired at recording level. The existing 12-row probes
are **not** 12 independent recordings. There is no standby or ramp acceptance
for DREGON.

**Michael's rig — fixed-recording gate on FLY124.** The population-level 95 %
criterion is explicitly **waived** by the user, because there is only one
held-out eight-channel recording. Equal regime weighting applies to the primary
MAE itself:

$$
E_{\text{rig}}
=\tfrac13\left(E_{\text{standby}}+E_{\text{ramp}}+E_{\text{cruise}}\right),
\qquad
\frac{E_{\text{rig,new}}}{E_{\text{rig,best}}}\le1.05 .
$$

Averaging the three per-regime **ratios** is explicitly rejected: that form
gives a tiny standby MAE disproportionate leverage and invites near-zero
denominators. Every regime and its own ratio are still reported separately, as
diagnostics. Any block uncertainty is conditional on FLY124 and is never an
across-recording population-95 claim. Fitting is on FLY125; FLY124 stays held
out for predictive checks.

**Separate gates.** An overlap-aware held-out **composite** improvement gate
(§6.2.3) and a **baseline-calibrated LTAS** gate are evaluated separately. No
percentage NLL is reported, ever.

**Both rigs.** The primary MAE uses the raw telemetry reference shared by all
arms; the realized shaft RPS MAE is diagnostic (§8.3). Training a tracker on
synthetic and testing it on real is out of scope. Comparing raw-initialized
inferred carrier corrections with the existing refined tracks is diagnostic
only: refined tracks are not ground truth, and disagreement is not automatic
failure. No spectral-fit claim may require the inferred correction to equal a
refined track.

# 13. Optional future complexity (not C2)

C2 is deliberately the smallest model and the smallest fitting
procedure that could satisfy the frozen criteria. Much of what follows was, in
an earlier version of this document, presented as the recommended framework.
It is now explicitly **optional future** work, governed by one rule.

:::: {.callout-important}
## One complexity, one named failure

Add exactly one scientifically motivated complexity, and only when a **named**
acceptance criterion has actually failed. Report conceptual complexity —
explicit stochastic mechanisms, independent parameter blocks and degrees of
freedom, latent states, inference stages and approximations — alongside any
score or runtime. A faster but opaque approximation is not automatically
simpler mathematically.
::::

Demoted from the recommendation:

- full complex state-space smoothing, the iterated Gaussian smoother, and the
  sparse MAP smoother stack;
- generalized-EM or Laplace hyperparameter updates;
- Kalman and structured-Kalman filtering, and any $O(K)$ complexity claim
  (§6.1.6);
- particle and Rao--Blackwellised particle smoothers;
- the crossing/overlap graph, temporal hysteresis, and nearest-component
  assignment;
- per-order free $D_{rk}$, the hierarchy
  $\log D_{rk}=d_{0}+d_{1}\log k+u_{k}$, and any order law;
- an exact Gaussian OU **bridge** covariance kernel (§8.4);
- a second shared physical process, a shared amplitude state, or a
  microphone-side phase process;
- the Stage C full joint refinement (§6.3).

The diagnostic triggers that would motivate one of them are unchanged. Curved
order-normalised residual structure functions point to a coloured or
mean-reverting residual process. More than one important eigenmode in the
off-diagonal covariance points to a second shared physical process, such as
structural vibration or common propagation jitter. Amplitudes co-varying across
orders point to a shared amplitude state, separate from phase. Microphone pairs
disagreeing after propagation correction point to a microphone-side process
rather than a changed source process. A setpoint-dependent shaft correlation
time points to hierarchical $\lambda_r(c)$ and $\sigma_{\nu,r}(c)$. Correlated
residual orders point to a low-rank-plus-diagonal residual covariance that
still retains the known shaft loading vector $k$ as a distinguished component.

# 14. New concise model statement

The following paragraph can replace the present high-level description of the
line model.

:::: {.callout-important}
**C2.** Each rotor's carrier is the **raw** telemetry trajectory,
delayed by $\delta_r$ and offset by a per-clip bias $b_{c,r}$ that is a random
effect with a proper prior and a population/recording mean, plus **one** shared
latent shaft state: an OU speed deviation $\nu_r$ and its exactly coupled
integral $\theta_r$, shared by every harmonic order and every microphone. Order
$k$ receives $k\theta_r$ plus an independent Wiener residual phase with **one
scalar diffusion $D_g$ per rig** — one number for every rotor and order, units
rad$^2$/s, no hidden $k$ scaling — whose initial phase is uniform on
$[0,2\pi)$ and shared across microphones.
$\lambda_g$ and $\sigma_g$ are rig-level, moment-initialized and then
frozen. The observation is the finite-window spectral mean with the latent path
integrated inside every moving-frame atom, fitted by **one** ordinary-Adam
plug-in composite MAP objective under one exact Gaussian integrated-OU state
prior. The renderer advances the same shared shaft state and the same
independent harmonic residuals, and emits the audio together with the realized
interval-average shaft rate. A narrow-plus-broad Cauchy fit remains a useful
descriptive baseline, but its weights are not interpreted as deterministic and
stochastic power fractions.
::::

1. Freeze the current two-Cauchy fit as a baseline. **Do not delete its
   results.** The refit on refined labels
   (`results/S2/cruise_8clip_refined.json`, fitted `k_half` 1.73-3.27) is part
   of that baseline.
2. Stop using $k_{1/2}$ as a physical coherence parameter in new experiments.
3. Freeze the evaluator baseline and the manifest first. **No candidate fit
   runs before the frozen baseline evaluator is approved.** Round 1 of at most
   eight begins only when it is explicitly authorized; the ledger is
   `docs/experiments/revised-phase-campaign.qmd`.
4. Extract complex phases from the existing Motor1_80 clip and run the
   rank-one covariance and order-normalised-difference diagnostics (§11,
   phase 1). Bench stays an optional planted/physical diagnostic, not a
   reported scientific candidate arm.
5. Benchmark the windowed-correlation kernel of §6.2.1 — not the
   intrinsic-table route whose prototype is timed in §6.5 — on the device that
   will run the fits, and validate it in the $\sigma_{\nu}\to0$ limit against
   the analytic Lorentzian.
6. Run the §9 checks that need no fit: exact transition moments, the zero-noise
   window response, exposure duplication, and the render round trip.
7. Only then fit C2 as specified in §6 and §7.1, and score it with the
   frozen evaluator.

This order of work is important. The cross-harmonic diagnostics are cheap and
directly test the new causal claim, and the gates mean nothing until the
instrument that reads them is frozen.
